document.title: Layout Graphs, Random Walks and the t-wise Independence of SPN Block Ciphers

candidate.title: 192-Round AES Is 2^-128-Close to Pairwise Independent
candidate.subtitle: Proved for AES with most mixing layers removed; conjectured for AES itself
candidate.one_line: 192-round AES with independent round keys is 2^-128-close to pairwise independent.
candidate.status_note: Theorem 7 proves the bound for '192-round censored AES' -- real AES S-boxes and mixing layer, but a subset of the mixing layers removed. The source conjectures the same round count suffices for AES itself, i.e. that censoring never increases security, and calls proving it an outstanding open problem. The best proved bound for actual AES is Liu-Tessaro-Vaikuntanathan's, needing more than 9000 rounds.
candidate.progress_note: 7-round AES* (random independent S-boxes, real AES mixing) reaches 2^-128 by Theorem 6; the 192 rounds are entirely the price of replacing a random S-box by sequential applications of the real one.

parameters.meaning: S-box input length and width; the block is 128 bits
round count; the conjecture fixes r = 192
statistical distance from pairwise independence; the target is 2^-128

candidate.why_interesting: A concrete, falsifiable claim about the actual AES design with its actual S-box, at a round count 47 times smaller than the best proved bound, resting on a monotonicity intuition nobody has been able to formalize.
candidate.why_clean: One cipher, one round count, one closeness parameter, all named numerically. Nothing asymptotic.

quotes.quote: We conjecture that 192-round of AES itself is also 2−128 -close to pairwise independent, i.e., the censoring mixing layers never increases security.
We view proving this conjecture formally to be an outstanding open problem.

If one believes that the mixing layers are useful for AES to achieve pseudorandomness, then it is natural to expect that removing a large fraction of them should only hurt the convergence to pairwise independence.
We give a censored variant of AES which is 2−128 -close to pairwise independent after 192 rounds.
This should be contrasted with [LTV21], which shows that AES is 2−128 -close to pairwise independent after (more than) 9000 rounds.
The 7-round AES∗ is 2−128 -close to pairwise independent.

check.notes: The conjecture is verbatim on page 7 with its rationale repeated on page 29 and the openness marker attached there. No repair was needed to the statement. Three contextual facts were added from elsewhere in the source and its predecessor, each grounded: Theorem 6's 7-round bound for AES*, the >9000-round prior bound for real AES, and the arithmetic by which 192 is reached. The independent-round-keys assumption is flagged prominently because the source states it and it is what separates the result from AES-128 as deployed.
